comments.text: Bruh, just have a go at RDR2 and that's pretty much the weapons system in GTAVI. You'll have an associate who will be able to bring your car to you, if you left it somewhere (to steal a car, or catch the train). I am really here for this new gameplay direction. In some ways, GTA 5 lowered the realism threshold in relation to the available technology, and inadvertently leaned on the outrageous, goofier side of things; it is the most "Saints Row like GTA", it is "The GTA" for the iPad baby generation. GTA VI was so dark, moody, and serious while still being a hilarious satire, yet retaining some classic gameplay liberties like an "unlimited weapon load out", at least one of each category... So although Niko can slip a rocket launcher out of his beautiful slavic colon, you couldn't have two types of submachine guns on person... This is overshadowed by the Euphoria Engine physics and driving, which was absolutely nerfed in GTA 5, and all of a sudden you could have an entire gun store in your pocket. This combination of interactive open world freedom, physics and graphics quality that better reflect the available technology make GTA VI very appealing to me over 5. Yeah, it is a risky move by Rockstar stepping away from GTA 5 gameplay styles, but GTA 5 is not going anywhere. I feel most who do not like the more realistic features of GTA IV and VI, they are likely to be those who enjoy GTA 5 Online. And those who prefer more realism seen in GTA IV and VI, are likely vary fond of the Read Dead series. Rockstar must have noticed they could not please everyone by rolling back features in 5 that were groundbreaking in VI, as those disappointed by 5 just weren't vocal about it at launch, so many were not ready for what we were given in GTA IV. With GTA VI they are changing direction to meet high expectations. At this point in time, If I had no idea, and saw gameplay comparisons between GTA 4 / 5 / 6, I would think GTA 5 looks like it precedes GTA 4, and GTA 6 is the culminate version.
comments.author: @jbones360

comments.text:
RDR2 had more or less the same weapon-carrying system, and that game is a masterpiece I still enjoy today. We can also stash guns in vehicle trunks, which is basically the same concept as using your horse as mobile weapon storage in RDR2.

I played GTA V yesterday and realized I rarely use more than 2 types of long guns and 2 types of pistols anyway. I usually stick with the best sidearm and long-range weapon, while most others barely get used. GTA V also gets boring fast because everything feels disposable, and once you finish the story and side content, there’s not much left to do.

More simulation in GTA VI can only make the gameplay more immersive. It’s still a video game, so you’ll always be able to do ridiculous things that aren’t realistic. My only concerns are leftist political influence leading to Orwellian restrictions or censorship that strip away GTA’s freedom and fun, and the possibility that Jason dies and we’re stuck playing as "girl-boss" Lucia after 100% completion.

comments.text:
They have been experimenting with differing amounts of realism for a while. GTA4 was a big one, the way NPCs fell or recoiled when shot, the way the cars handled... Many loved it, many hated it, but people forget about those details when they are looking back at the games. They scaled those back a bit for GTAV, but with how the realism of RDR2 was received so well, it isn't a surprising move.
And the people complaining about not being able to hold every weapon in the game, did y'all not play anything before GTAV? Because in all the previous GTA games you could only carry ONE weapon of each type at a time. And dying or getting arrested got all your guns taken away. I think a hybrid of these two systems would work well, so maybe you can only hold a few weapons at a time, but dying or being arrested makes you lose WHAT YOU WERE CARRYING. So you wont lose your entire arsenal and will actually be thankful for the limited inventory.
